target_icp: Founders, COOs, and operations leaders at scaling beauty, wellness, premium CPG, and beverage brands
buying_trigger: Missed production windows, inconsistent quality, capacity limits, reformulation, or IP concerns
core_thesis: Co-man selection must test capability, capacity, controls, communication, and commercial fit—not just unit price.
key_elements: Readiness brief; RFQ inputs; capability and capacity screen; audit questions; pilot process; quality agreement; IP/tooling ownership; lead-time validation; scorecard; transition plan
proof_to_include: Founder evidence on variable lead times and opaque intermediaries; anonymized failure patterns; scorecard; cost-of-delay scenario
objections_to_address: We already have a co-man; a broker handles this; audits slow launch; overseas is always cheaper
soft_cta: Use the scorecard to pressure-test your current or shortlisted co-man.

target_icp: Founders, COOs, finance leads, and demand planners at omnichannel brands
buying_trigger: Stockouts alongside excess inventory, wholesale launch, long lead times, or cash trapped in slow SKUs
core_thesis: Forecasting is a cross-functional operating cadence that protects service levels and cash together.
key_elements: Channel inputs; bottoms-up forecast; SKU segmentation; lead-time/MOQ assumptions; safety stock; launch scenarios; open-to-buy; accuracy and bias; operating cadence; ownership map
proof_to_include: SEEQ and Dossier founder quotes; over-order scenario; cash-conversion example; downloadable model
objections_to_address: Sales is unpredictable; we are too early for S&OP; software solves it; more inventory is safer
soft_cta: Model one high-risk SKU before the next purchase order.

target_icp: Founders, CFOs, and COOs adding wholesale, retail, international, or complex fulfillment
buying_trigger: Revenue rises while cash and contribution margin weaken
core_thesis: Gross margin hides the operational leakage that determines whether growth creates or consumes cash.
key_elements: Landed-cost waterfall; duties/freight; packaging/assembly; 3PL; deductions; returns/damage; trade spend; channel contribution; SKU/customer profitability; review cadence
proof_to_include: Channel comparison; packaging-cube example; anonymized cost waterfall; authorized case metrics where relevant
objections_to_address: Our gross margin is healthy; finance tracks this; freight is temporary; volume offsets leakage
soft_cta: Run one hero SKU through the full cost-to-serve waterfall.

target_icp: Founders, COOs, sourcing leaders, and quality leaders in beauty, wellness, hardware, and spirits
buying_trigger: Single-source dependency, recurring defects, certification surprises, or communication failures
core_thesis: Resilience is designed through specifications, contracts, testing, alternates, and escalation rules before failure.
key_elements: Dependency map; critical-component risk; approved specs; quality agreement; inspection/testing; change notification; certifications; capacity health; secondary sourcing; corrective actions; escalation tree
proof_to_include: Hardware supplier-dependency quote; beauty compatibility examples; defect-cost scenario; risk matrix
objections_to_address: A second source costs more; the relationship is strong; contracts cannot prevent defects; quality systems are overhead
soft_cta: Map the three supplier failures that could stop revenue this quarter.

target_icp: Founders, COOs, sales leaders, and operations teams preparing for major retail or distribution
buying_trigger: Authorization arrives before systems and cash are ready
core_thesis: Getting on shelf is a commercial win; staying there requires inventory, compliance, data, fulfillment, and cash readiness before the first PO.
key_elements: Readiness gates; unit economics; forecast/PO plan; onboarding; EDI/ASNs; routing guides; packaging/labeling; deductions; distributor terms; promotional inventory; velocity review; 30/60/90 plan
proof_to_include: Retail-buyer and founder quotes; checklist; first-PO cash scenario; beauty, hardware, and beverage examples
objections_to_address: The broker handles it; retailer forecasts are enough; compliance can wait; we will fix issues after launch
soft_cta: Pressure-test the operating plan before accepting the launch date.

target_icp: Founders, COOs, and ecommerce or operations leaders outgrowing a warehouse or incumbent 3PL
buying_trigger: Weak visibility, rising errors or damage, retail requirements, kitting, or poor returns handling
core_thesis: A 3PL should be selected against the brand's operating model and next channel—not a generic rate card.
key_elements: Order/SKU profile; B2B versus DTC; WMS/integrations; SLAs; accuracy; kitting; lot/expiry control; returns; retail compliance; peak capacity; implementation; exit terms; RFP scorecard
proof_to_include: Dossier specialization evidence; damage/returns examples; weighted RFP; total-cost comparison
objections_to_address: All 3PLs are similar; cheapest pick fee wins; Shopify integration is enough; switching is too risky
soft_cta: Use the requirements matrix before requesting another 3PL quote.

target_icp: Beauty founders, COOs, operations leaders, and product-development teams
buying_trigger: SKU proliferation, retail expansion, formula-pack incompatibility, claims pressure, or component lead times
core_thesis: Beauty operations must coordinate formula, components, claims, suppliers, testing, inventory, and launch timing as one system.
key_elements: Compatibility; critical path; decoration/artwork; stability/transit testing; batch control; claims/retailer standards; MOQ alignment; sampling; change control; SKU rationalization
proof_to_include: Junk Theory, FROST, Daybird, and Dossier quotes; launch critical path; compatibility scenario; authorized Epicutis metrics
objections_to_address: The lab handles packaging; the designer owns artwork; vendors manage timing; every SKU needs unique packaging
soft_cta: Map formula, pack, claims, and inventory dependencies on one launch calendar.

target_icp: Founders, COOs, hardware program managers, and supply-chain leaders in electronics, wearables, health tech, and babytech
buying_trigger: Long commitments, certification risk, supplier concentration, retail launch, or high returns
core_thesis: Hardware scale needs control across engineering changes, suppliers, compliance, inventory, packaging, and channel launch.
key_elements: Long-lead planning; BOM/revision control; tooling/capacity; certification/claims; incoming quality; protective packaging/setup; retail display/theft; warranty/returns; forecast scenarios; launch gates
proof_to_include: Hardware-founder and Retailbound evidence; authorized Audio Enhancement metrics; risk matrix
objections_to_address: The contract manufacturer owns operations; certification is engineering; more inventory protects launch; packaging is cosmetic
soft_cta: Identify the certification, supplier, or component that can move the launch date.

target_icp: Founders, COOs, sourcing, packaging, and logistics leaders across premium products
buying_trigger: Packaging cost rises, damage persists, freight cube is high, or requirements change
core_thesis: Packaging engineering changes margin, freight, quality, throughput, compliance, and experience simultaneously.
key_elements: System cost versus unit price; dimensions/cube; structure; line compatibility; pack-out labor; damage testing; palletization; retail compliance; sustainability; specification control; transition
proof_to_include: Authorized Audio Enhancement and Artilect metrics; cost waterfall; before/after architecture
objections_to_address: Redesign risks the brand; savings are too small; sustainability costs more; supplier owns specs
soft_cta: Evaluate one package on total system cost, not piece price.

target_icp: Founders, CEOs, investors, and finance leaders deciding how to add operating capacity
buying_trigger: Founder remains the escalation point, hiring is slow, and problems span several specialties
core_thesis: The choice is which operating model provides accountable execution at the brand's current complexity and risk.
key_elements: Readiness signals; ownership scope; hire cost/time; fractional versus project versus embedded; specialties; governance; transition; 90-day outcomes; when to hire internally
proof_to_include: Current economics only after confirmation; workload scenarios; responsibility matrix; founder-capacity evidence; authorized outcomes
objections_to_address: Outside teams lack context; we need one owner; retainers get expensive; wait until after the raise
soft_cta: Compare the next 12 months of operating needs—not just one salary line.

target_icp: Brand directors, marketing leaders, founders, and packaging leads in beauty, wellness, luxury, and premium products
buying_trigger: Retail launch, rebrand, weak shelf recognition, or inability to justify premium price
core_thesis: Retail packaging must communicate category, benefit, brand, and price point in seconds while surviving operational constraints.
key_elements: Shelf audit; category codes; hierarchy/claims; size/silhouette; color/finish; primary-secondary relationship; retailer requirements; accessibility; transit integrity; testing; iteration
proof_to_include: Daybird and Doosra quotes; shelf audit; verified retailer evidence; before/after mockups
objections_to_address: Great design stands out alone; DTC transfers to retail; more claims improve conversion; premium means more material
soft_cta: Audit the pack at shelf distance before approving the next print run.

target_icp: Beauty founders and product-development, brand, or packaging leaders
buying_trigger: Formula, dispensing, components, artwork, and timing move separately
core_thesis: Beauty packaging succeeds when compatibility, experience, design, suppliers, and production develop together from the start.
key_elements: Product brief; formula/dosage; primary pack/dispensing; compatibility/stability; decoration; secondary structure; claims/artwork; samples/color standards; MOQ/lead time; filling-line fit; testing; change control
proof_to_include: Junk Theory and FROST quotes; Dossier standardization; compatibility examples; development timeline
objections_to_address: Packaging comes after formula; stock components eliminate testing; every SKU needs a custom pack
soft_cta: Bring packaging into the critical path before formula and launch dates are locked.

target_icp: Founders and sustainability, brand, innovation, or packaging leaders
buying_trigger: Sustainability goals, retailer mandates, EPR pressure, or consumer scrutiny
core_thesis: Credible sustainability is a documented tradeoff across reduction, reuse, material, manufacturing, transport, recovery, and claims.
key_elements: Waste hierarchy; baseline; lifecycle boundaries; lightweighting; recycled content; mono-materials; refill/reuse feasibility; recovery; certifications; substantiation; EPR/PPWR; testing
proof_to_include: Formula Botanica and PMMI evidence; ecoSPIRITS example; material comparison; claims checklist
objections_to_address: Recyclable means sustainable; refill is always better; glass is greener; sustainability destroys luxury
soft_cta: Choose the sustainability outcome first, then design the package and claim around it.

target_icp: Founders and brand, packaging, procurement, or product-development leaders
buying_trigger: Concept fails quoting, MOQ exceeds demand, lead time threatens launch, or line incompatibility appears late
core_thesis: Design must be engineered for the actual supplier, process, equipment, volume, labor, and landed-cost target.
key_elements: Volume/forecast; target cost; process; dielines/tolerances; materials/finishes; tooling; capability; MOQ; sampling; line compatibility; QC; lead time; freight; scale path; change control
proof_to_include: Greg Berguig and Matt Craighead quotes; MOQ scenarios; sample-to-production gates; landed-cost example
objections_to_address: Any printer can make it; prototypes prove manufacturability; lower MOQ is always better
soft_cta: Pressure-test the concept against volume, equipment, and target landed cost before final art.

target_icp: Brand marketing, PR, influencer, experiential, and agency leads across aligned categories
buying_trigger: Product launch, seeding, press moment, collaboration, or holiday activation
core_thesis: A high-performing kit is a designed content experience serving one campaign objective through reveal, messaging, protection, kitting, and production.
key_elements: Audience/action; filming context; opening sequence; hierarchy/story; fit/protection; inserts; personalization; privacy; assembly/fulfillment; quantity tiers; timeline; measurement
proof_to_include: Logic Pac low-MOQ capability; verified unboxing evidence; campaign brief; measured-outcome evidence marked as a gap
objections_to_address: Bigger boxes earn more posts; every recipient needs the same kit; ROI cannot be measured
soft_cta: Define the moment you want creators to film before designing the structure.

target_icp: Founders and creative, brand, packaging, or ecommerce leaders in luxury categories
buying_trigger: Premium repositioning, gifting, retail expansion, or packaging that does not match price
core_thesis: Luxury comes from coherence, restraint, tactility, structure, pacing, sound, and service—not simply heavier materials.
key_elements: Price context; brand codes; sensory hierarchy; materials/finishes; reveal; protection; gifting; shipper; theft/returns; accessibility; repeat-order path; sustainability; consistency
proof_to_include: Evelio Mattos quote; fragrance/jewelry sources; teardown; first-order versus replenishment economics
objections_to_address: Luxury requires weight; sustainability weakens premium; more layers create value
soft_cta: Identify the three details that must carry the premium impression and remove the rest.

target_icp: Sustainability, innovation, packaging, operations, and brand leaders in beauty and spirits
buying_trigger: Refill/reuse commitment, packaging fees, retailer program, or single-use reduction goal
core_thesis: Refill only works when protection, behavior, return logistics, cleaning, tracking, economics, and communication form a system.
key_elements: Use case/geography; architecture; reuse threshold; compatibility/hygiene; behavior; collection; cleaning; reverse logistics; retailer role; tracking; cost/use; loss; claims
proof_to_include: ecoSPIRITS and beauty-refill evidence; system map; break-even scenario; regional limitations
objections_to_address: Consumers will return it; refill automatically lowers impact; one model works everywhere
soft_cta: Model the complete return loop before engineering the refill component.

target_icp: Founders and brand, regulatory, packaging, and ecommerce leaders
buying_trigger: New efficacy/sustainability claim, retailer onboarding, EPR change, or redesign
core_thesis: Claims need evidence, hierarchy, market rules, retailer standards, and end-of-life reality before artwork approval.
key_elements: Claim inventory; substantiation owner; regulatory versus marketing language; retailer standards; recyclability/disposal; certifications; symbols; hierarchy; variants; approval; change log
proof_to_include: Daybird quote; greenwashing/EPR sources; claims matrix; retailer checklist
objections_to_address: Small brands are not scrutinized; supplier certificates suffice; recyclable claims are universal
soft_cta: Create the claim-evidence matrix before the design review.

target_icp: Founders and product marketing, industrial design, packaging engineering, and retail leaders in headphones, wearables, health tech, and babytech
buying_trigger: Retail launch, high returns, plastic-reduction goal, confusing setup, or premium repositioning
core_thesis: Hardware packaging must protect, teach setup, satisfy retail security, reduce returns, and feel premium without avoidable cube or plastic.
key_elements: Device/accessory architecture; protection tests; opening/setup; cable organization; safety cues; anti-theft/display; ecommerce versus retail; cube; paper retention; accessibility; returns feedback; revisions
proof_to_include: Retailbound/hardware evidence; authorized Audio Enhancement metric; damage/setup scenario; teardown
objections_to_address: Industrial design owns experience; more foam is safer; QR codes replace instructions; one pack fits all channels
soft_cta: Design the first five minutes of ownership alongside the protective structure.

target_icp: Founders and brand, sustainability, packaging, or operations leaders at premium wine and spirits brands
buying_trigger: Glass cost/weight, new format, DTC growth, retailer mandate, reuse initiative, or premium repositioning
core_thesis: A format transition must preserve premium cues while proving protection, production fit, channel acceptance, understanding, and logistics economics.
key_elements: Baseline; bottle weight/cube; alternatives; closures/barrier; labels/decoration; filling-line fit; case/pallet; DTC protection; channel objections; education; EPR/DRS/PPWR; pilot
proof_to_include: Packamama and ecoSPIRITS quotes; Juliet evidence; freight comparison; premium-cue audit
objections_to_address: Glass is required for premium; distributors resist change; weight signals quality
soft_cta: Pilot one channel and prove economics and perception before a full portfolio change.
